In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
leukemia is a disease that is caused by genetic lesions that produce a block of differentiation.

the genetic lesions of leukemia, resulting in a block of maturation, can be reversed by specific inhibitors of the genetic lesions that allow the leukemic cells either to differentiate and undergo terminal differentiation or to undergo apoptosis.
the leukemias represent a model of the maturation arrest of normal cells, and that the genetic lesions of leukemia are amenable to differentiation therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the genetic lesion of leukemia is a block in differentiation (maturation) that can be reversed by specific inhibitors of the genetically altered protein products.
we have developed a model system to study the effects of the genetic lesions in leukemia and have identified several potential therapeutic agents that may be useful in the treatment of leukemia.
the genetic lesions of leukemias result in a block in differentiation (maturation) of the leukemic cell that allows these cells to continue to replicate.
